name: Touraine

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Touraine whites are dry and mainly Sauvignon Blanc, with citrus, tropical fruit or white flower aromas and a fresh finish.
Touraine reds are based on Côt, or on Cabernet Franc west of Tours, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Gamay and Pinot Noir also allowed.

blurb.text: A broad Loire Valley appellation for white, red and rosé wines, with sparkling white and rosé also allowed. Most of it is white, and the reds range from light, fruity Gamay to firmer Cabernet Franc wines and blends. It covers the same ground as many smaller local appellations.
